_comment: The US retail and holiday calendar the audience actually works to.
A buyer in the States is not thinking about our factory in September; they
are thinking about the reset that has to be on the floor before Halloween
and the container that has to land before Black Friday. A post timed to
that reads as someone who knows their year.
'kind' decides how the calendar draws it and whether it can carry a post:
holiday  — a federal holiday. Marked on the calendar; nothing is posted
on one, and the planner treats it as a blackout.
retail   — a selling moment. Marked, and a post may be timed to it.
ours     — HOMEDANT's own dates, which come from brand.json.
'lead_days' is how far ahead the buying conversation happens: a post about
Black Friday storage in late November is too late to sell anything.

moments.name: Back to School winds down
moments.angle: The dorm and classroom orders are placed and installed. What the buildings learned about their storage this year is what they will specify next year.

moments.name: Halloween
moments.angle: Decorations come out of storage and go back into it three weeks later. The bins have to live somewhere for the other eleven months.

moments.name: Black Friday
moments.angle: The stock for this week landed in September. A reset date does not move because a vessel did, which is what domestic warehousing is for.

moments.name: Small Business Saturday
moments.angle: An independent retailer resets a bay with what fits on one pallet, not one container.

moments.name: Cyber Monday
moments.angle: Every online order is a box that leaves a back room. The back room is the constraint nobody merchandises.

moments.name: Boxing week returns
moments.angle: The week after Christmas is the year's biggest sort: returns in, decorations away, garages emptied out in January.
